records.title: Dependencies module (FS/SS/FF/SF)
records.body:
## Parent

https://github.com/TanStack/time/issues/25

## What to build

Extract the FS/SS/FF/SF event dependency system into a proper module. When registered, the module adds dependency-aware transformation to the write pipeline: moving a predecessor event automatically cascades the required shift to all dependents in topological order.

This module is the reason the Timeline/Gantt view exists as a product. Extracting it from \`CalendarCore\` into a module also fixes the current architecture where Gantt semantics are baked into the Calendar kernel.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] \`DependenciesModule\` plugs into the kernel via the module API (#28)
- [ ] \`createDependency(sourceId, targetId, type)\` creates a link and validates it does not form a cycle
- [ ] Moving a predecessor cascades the correct shift to all dependents (FS: finish-to-start, SS: start-to-start, FF: finish-to-finish, SF: start-to-finish)
- [ ] Cascade propagates transitively through the dependency graph in topological order
- [ ] \`validateEventDependencies()\` checks whether placing an event satisfies its predecessor constraints
- [ ] Circular dependency detection rejects the link with a descriptive error before it is committed
- [ ] Removing the \`DependenciesModule\` causes dependency code to tree-shake out of the bundle

## Blocked by

https://github.com/TanStack/time/issues/28

records.title: Packaging & distribution: version duplication, dependency drift, console-window GUI entry, fragile run.bat, no installer
records.body:
# Packaging & distribution: version duplication, dep drift, console-window GUI entry, fragile run.bat, no end-user install story

## Problems

1. **Version is declared twice**: `pyproject.toml` (`version = "0.1.0"`) and `hdrshot/__init__.py` (`__version__ = "0.1.0"`). They will drift. Single-source it (keep pyproject as truth, expose via `importlib.metadata.version("hdrshot")`, or use `[project] dynamic = ["version"]` + `[tool.setuptools.dynamic]`).

2. **`requirements.txt` duplicates `pyproject.toml` dependencies** with identical loose ranges — two sources of truth and no reproducibility. Recommendation: `pyproject.toml` stays the abstract spec; replace `requirements.txt` with a pinned lock (`uv lock`/`pip-compile`) used by `run.bat` and CI so "works on my machine" is testable.

3. **GUI launches through a console entry point.** `[project.scripts] hdrshot = ...` means an installed `hdrshot.exe` opens a console window behind the Qt UI. Add `[project.gui-scripts] hdrshot-gui = "hdrshot.__main__:main"` (pythonw-based) and keep the console script for the CLI subcommands.

4. **`run.bat` failure modes**:
   - Uses bare `python` from PATH — on a clean Windows box that's the Microsoft Store stub or possibly a too-old interpreter; no `>=3.10` check even though `pyproject.toml` requires it.
   - First-run logic is `if not exist .venv\Scripts\python.exe` — if `pip install` fails halfway (e.g. network drop), the venv exists, so **every subsequent run skips installation and launches a broken app**. Use a sentinel/marker written only after a successful install, and check `pip install` exit codes.
   - `pip install` output isn't checked at all (`errorlevel` ignored).

5. **No end-user distribution.** The target audience for "better Snipping Tool" is not people with Python installed. Plan:
   - [ ] CI job building a **PyInstaller** onedir bundle (onedir, not onefile — Qt + numpy onefile extraction is slow and antivirus-prone), attached to GitHub Releases with a version tag.
   - [ ] **winget** manifest once releases are stable.
   - [ ] Note: unsigned exes trip SmartScreen; document it, consider signing later.
   - [ ] Keep LGPL (PySide6) and GPL (x265/HEIC — see the licensing issue) constraints in mind for what gets bundled.

6. **Install weight / extras.** PySide6 is a ~200 MB dependency that the headless CLI (`full`, `region`, `selftest`) doesn't need. Consider extras: base install = capture + encoders, `hdrshot[gui]` adds PySide6, `hdrshot[heic]` adds pillow-heif. `pipeline.py` already lazy-imports heic; the GUI import is already isolated to `ui/`.

7. Missing package metadata for a public release: `py.typed` marker (the code is well-typed), PyPI classifiers, `project.urls`, and a `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Suggested order

Items 1–4 are small and immediate; 5–7 ride on the CI work in the testing issue.

records.title: [build-timings] Build Performance Report — 2026-07-15
records.body:
## Build Summary

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| **Date** | 2026-07-15 |
| **Total build time** | **220s (3m 40s)** — cold build from `cargo clean` |
| **Compilation units** | 372 total (336 compiled, 36 build scripts) |
| **Compiler** | rustc 1.97.0 (2d8144b78 2026-07-07) |
| **Cargo** | 1.97.0 (c980f4866 2026-06-30) |
| **Profile** | `dev` (unoptimized + debuginfo) |
| **Clippy** | ✅ 0 warnings |

---

## Top 5 Slowest Compilation Units

| # | Unit | Version | Total | Type | Key Features |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `aws-lc-sys` | 0.40.0 | **91.5s** | build-script (run) | `prebuilt-nasm` |
| 2 | `libgit2-sys` | 0.17.0+1.8.1 | **72.8s** | build-script (run) | `https`, `openssl-sys` |
| 3 | `syn` | 2.0.117 | **27.8s** | compile | `full`, `derive`, `extra-traits`, `fold`, `visit` |
| 4 | `rustls` | 0.23.37 | **23.8s** | compile | `ring`, `log`, `tls12` |
| 5 | `jsonschema` | 0.46.4 | **22.7s** | compile | `reqwest`, `resolve-http`, `resolve-file`, `tls-aws-lc-rs` |

Additional notable compile times: `rustls` (aws-lc-rs variant) 22.6s · `reqwest` 19.9s · `regex-automata` 17.9s (×2) · `clap_builder` 14.0s · `ring` build script 12.4s · `serde_derive` 12.9s · `toml_edit` 12.7s

### Critical Path

`syn` is the most significant bottleneck on the dependency graph — it directly unblocks **15 downstream compilation units** (all proc-macro crates that depend on it: `serde_derive`, `clap_derive`, `thiserror-impl`, `tokio-macros`, etc.). Anything that reduces `syn`'s compile time (or parallelism with it) has outsized impact.

---

## Dependency Analysis

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| **Direct dependencies** (depth 1) | ~43 |
| **Total compilation units** | 372 |
| **Duplicate crate versions** | 2 (`bitflags` v1.3.2 and v2.11.0) |

### Duplicate Crate Versions

```
bitflags v1.3.2  →  lsp-types v0.94.1  →  tower-lsp v0.20.0
bitflags v2.11.0 →  (workspace direct + libaipm-engine-spec)
```

`lsp-types` is pinned to the old bitflags 1.x API. This forces two different `bitflags` versions to be compiled. This is a known upstream issue with `tower-lsp`/`lsp-types`.

### TLS Backend Duplication

Two versions of `rustls` are compiled — one with the `ring` crypto backend and one with `aws-lc-rs`:

- `rustls` (ring) — pulled by `reqwest` (via HTTP client in `ureq` path / `hyper-rustls`)
- `rustls` (aws-lc-rs) — pulled by `jsonschema`'s `tls-aws-lc-rs` feature via `reqwest`

This doubles the TLS compilation cost and triggers the extremely slow `aws-lc-sys` C build (91.5s).

---

## Cargo Lint Findings

- **Clippy**: ✅ Zero warnings — all `deny`/`warn` lints pass cleanly.
- **`multiple_crate_versions`**: Set to `allow` in `Cargo.toml` (appropriate — `bitflags` dual-version is forced by `lsp-types` upstream).
- **`cargo` lint group**: ✅ Enabled at `warn` level.
- No unused dependency lints triggered.

---

## Recommendations

### 🔴 High Impact

**1. Disable `jsonschema`'s `resolve-http` and `tls-aws-lc-rs` features**

The `jsonschema` crate is currently compiled with `reqwest`, `resolve-http`, `resolve-file`, and `tls-aws-lc-rs`. This single dependency pulls in the entire `reqwest` → `rustls` → `aws-lc-rs` → `aws-lc-sys` chain, causing the 91.5s C compilation. If HTTP schema resolution is not used at runtime (e.g., `$ref` URIs that point to external HTTP endpoints are never validated), disabling these features would eliminate the longest bottleneck.

```toml
# In workspace Cargo.toml — replace:
jsonschema = "0.46"
# With:
jsonschema = { version = "0.46", default-features = false, features = ["resolve-file"] }
```

Estimated savings: **~115s** (91.5s aws-lc-sys + 22.7s jsonschema recompile with fewer deps + one rustls variant).

**2. Unify TLS backend across `reqwest` and `jsonschema`**

Even if HTTP resolution in `jsonschema` is needed, ensure both `reqwest` (used by `ureq`/HTTP clients) and `jsonschema` use the **same** TLS backend. Currently ring and aws-lc-rs are both compiled. Pick one — if `aws-lc-rs` is preferred (FIPS compliance), configure `reqwest` explicitly. If `ring` is preferred, pin `jsonschema` to the ring feature.

Estimated savings: **~22-24s** (eliminates one redundant `rustls` compilation).

### 🟡 Medium Impact

**3. Reduce `syn` feature surface**

`syn` is compiled with every optional feature enabled (`full`, `extra-traits`, `fold`, `visit`, `visit-mut`). These are pulled in by various proc-macro crates. Some proc-macros (e.g., `serde_derive`, `thiserror-impl`) don't require `fold` or `visit-mut`. This is hard to control without forking, but worth auditing which of your direct proc-macro dependencies require the full feature set.

Estimated savings: **5-10s** if feature reduction is achievable upstream.

**4. Upgrade `lsp-types` / `tower-lsp` to unify `bitflags`**

The `bitflags` v1/v2 duplication adds minor compile overhead. Watch for a `lsp-types` release that migrates to `bitflags` 2.x, then upgrade `tower-lsp`.

Estimated savings: **minor** (< 1s on incremental builds, reduces total crate count by 1).

### 🟢 Low Impact / Already Optimized

- ✅ `git2` SSH disabled — saves ~8.7s per existing comment in `Cargo.toml`
- ✅ `profile.dev.package."*"` opt-level=1 for third-party — helps `libgit2-sys` and C-heavy crates cache better
- ✅ `debug = 1` (line tables only) — correct for dev builds
- ✅ `split-debuginfo = "unpacked"` — faster linking on Linux
- ✅ `inquire` with `default-features = false` — avoids unnecessary TUI backends

---

## Trend

| Report Date | Total Time | Compiler | Units | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-05-07 ([#831](https://github.com/TheLarkInn/aipm/issues/831)) | 220s | rustc 1.95.0 | 93 reported | Older unit count metric |
| 2026-07-13 ([#1236](https://github.com/TheLarkInn/aipm/issues/1236)) | 216s | rustc 1.97.0 | 372 | Stable |
| **2026-07-15 (this report)** | **220s** | **rustc 1.97.0** | **372** | **Stable — within noise** |

**Verdict: Build time is stable.** The 4s increase vs the 2026-07-13 report is within measurement noise (machine load variation). No new

records.title: [build-timings] Build Performance Report — 2026-07-28
records.body:
## Build Summary

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| **Date** | 2026-07-28 |
| **Total build time** | **228s (3m 47s)** — cold build from `cargo clean` |
| **Compilation units** | 372 total (372 dirty, 0 fresh) |
| **Max concurrency** | 6 |
| **Compiler** | rustc 1.97.1 (8bab26f4f 2026-07-14) |
| **Cargo** | 1.97.1 (c980f4866 2026-06-30) |
| **Profile** | `dev` (unoptimized + debuginfo) |
| **Clippy** | ✅ 0 warnings, 0 errors |

---

## Top 5 Slowest Compilation Units

| Rank | Unit | Total | Codegen | Key Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `aws-lc-sys` v0.40.0 (build-script run) | **93.5s** | — | C/NASM crypto library; pulled in by `jsonschema` → `reqwest` |
| 2 | `libgit2-sys` v0.17.0+1.8.1 (build-script run) | **75.2s** | — | libgit2 C library; already uses `https`-only (no SSH) |
| 3 | `syn` v2.0.117 | **27.1s** | — | Shared proc-macro dependency; no easy mitigation |
| 4 | `rustls` v0.23.37 | **23.4s** | — | Compiled with `aws-lc-rs` backend for `reqwest`/`jsonschema` |
| 5 | `jsonschema` v0.46.4 | **22.9s** | — | Pulls in heavy TLS/HTTP stack (`reqwest` + `aws-lc-rs`) |

> ⚠️ `aws-lc-sys` (93.5s) + `libgit2-sys` (75.2s) account for **73%** of the total wall-clock time and sit on the critical path.

---

## Dependency Analysis

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| **Total compilation units** | 372 |
| **Direct workspace deps (aipm crate, depth=1)** | 17 |
| **Duplicate crate versions** | **9 crates** with multiple versions |

### Duplicate Crates

| Crate | Versions | Root Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `bitflags` | v1.3.2, v2.11.0 | v1 pinned by `lsp-types` → `tower-lsp` |
| `derive_more` | v0.99.20, v2.1.1 | v0 pulled in by `cucumber` (dev dep) |
| `getrandom` | v0.2.17, v0.3.4, v0.4.2 | **Three versions** spread across crypto/rand crates |
| `hashbrown` | v0.14.5, v0.16.1 | v0.14 pulled in by `dashmap` → `tower-lsp` |
| `heck` | v0.4.1, v0.5.0 | v0.4 pulled in by `cucumber` (dev dep) |
| `openssl-probe` | v0.1.6, v0.2.1 | Both versions from OpenSSL/TLS chain |
| `regex-syntax` | v0.7.5, v0.8.10 | v0.7 pulled in by `cucumber-expressions` (dev dep) |
| `thiserror` | v1.0.69, v2.0.18 | v1 pulled in by `gherkin` → `cucumber` (dev dep) |
| `tower` | v0.4.13, v0.5.3 | v0.4 pinned by `tower-lsp`; v0.5 via `reqwest`/`jsonschema` |

---

## Cargo Lint Findings

- ✅ **Clippy**: zero warnings, zero errors — clean pass with `-D warnings`
- ✅ **Profile config**: `[profile.dev]` is well-configured (`opt-level=0`, `debug=1`, `split-debuginfo="unpacked"`, deps at `opt-level=1`)
- ⚠️ **`multiple_crate_versions`** is set to `allow` — duplicates above suppressed in CI; use `cargo tree --duplicates` to monitor
- i️ `jsonschema` workspace dep uses default features which activate `tls-aws-lc-rs` — root cause of the 93.5s `aws-lc-sys` compile

---

## ⚡ Recommendations

### 🔴 HIGH — Switch `jsonschema` to `tls-ring` backend (~70–90s potential saving)

`jsonschema` → `reqwest` pulls in `aws-lc-rs` by default. Switching to the `ring`-based TLS backend would eliminate the 93.5s `aws-lc-sys` build-script run:

```toml
# In Cargo.toml [workspace.dependencies]:
jsonschema = { version = "0.46", default-features = false, features = ["tls-ring"] }
```

`ring` is already compiled for `ureq` (the HTTP client used by `libaipm`), so this would reuse the existing build artifact.

### 🔴 HIGH — Upgrade `tower-lsp` to resolve `bitflags`/`hashbrown`/`tower` duplicates

`tower-lsp v0.20.0` pins `bitflags` v1, `hashbrown` v0.14, and `tower` v0.4. Upgrading or patching `tower-lsp` would unify these and reduce compile units. Check if v0.21+ is available or use a `[patch]` override.

### 🟡 MEDIUM — Update `lsp-types` to drop `bitflags` v1 dependency

`lsp-types v0.94.1` depends on `bitflags` v1.3.2. A newer version of `lsp-types` may have migrated to v2. Eliminates one duplicate compilation unit.

### 🟡 MEDIUM — Audit `cucumber` dev dependency for transitive bloat

`cucumber` (dev dep only) pulls in three old crate versions: `derive_more` v0, `heck` v0.4, `regex-syntax` v0.7, `thiserror` v1. These add test-binary-only compile time. Check whether a newer version of `cucumber` (v0.22+) has consolidated these.

### 🟢 LOW — Consider `mold` or `lld` linker for faster linking in dev builds

Add to `.cargo/config.toml`:
```toml
[target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu]
linker = "clang"
rustflags = ["-C", "link-arg=-fuse-ld=lld"]
```

Linking is a serial phase; a faster linker can cut 5–15s off dev build times.

---

## 📈 Trend (vs. Previous Report)

| Metric | 2026-07-27 (#1295) | 2026-07-28 (this) | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Total build time** | 232.3s | 228.0s | ✅ **−4.3s (−1.9%)** |
| **Compilation units** | 372 | 372 | — (stable) |
| **Max concurrency** | 5 | 6 | ✅ +1 (more parallelism) |
| **`aws-lc-sys` build** | 88.2s | 93.5s | ⚠️ +5.3s (system load variance) |
| **`libgit2-sys` build** | 73.2s | 75.2s | ⚠️ +2.0s (system load variance) |
| **Clippy** | ✅ clean | ✅ clean | — (stable) |

**Conclusion**: Build time is marginally improved at 228s. The dependency graph is unchanged (372 units). The C-compilation bottlenecks (`aws-lc-sys`, `libgit2-sys`) remain the dominant cost. The top recommendation from #1295 (switch `jsonschema` to `tls-ring`) has not yet been implemented and remains the highest-impact action available.

records.title: Separate runtime and dev/build code to fix large bundle & dependency graph
records.body:
### Problem

`intlayer` currently exposes build-time and development tooling through the same entrypoints used at runtime.

Because of this, importing very small features pulls large parts of the ecosystem into the dependency graph.

Examples observed in a Next.js production project:

| Import | Added to graph |
|------|------|
`import type { IntlayerConfig } from "intlayer"` | ~111 KB (≈39 KB gz) |
`import { withIntlayer } from "next-intlayer/server"` | ~1.6 MB gz |

The reason is architectural rather than optimization:

- The main `intlayer` package depends on CLI/config/compiler modules
- The Next.js helper (`withIntlayer`) also performs build/watch responsibilities
- Dev tooling (watchers, generators, filesystem loaders) becomes reachable from runtime entrypoints
- Bundlers and analyzers cannot reliably tree-shake these paths

Even if some code executes only in Node, exposing it through runtime entrypoints:
- inflates dependency graphs
- increases install/build time
- risks accidental bundling in edge/serverless environments
- makes performance analysis confusing

---

### Root Cause

There is no strict separation between:

| Layer | Should be |
|------|------|
Runtime (browser/server execution) | minimal, stable |
Server helpers | node-only |
Build/dev tooling | isolated |
CLI | isolated |

Currently these responsibilities are mixed across `intlayer` and `next-intlayer/server`.

---

### Proposed Solution

Introduce explicit entrypoint separation:

```
intlayer/
  runtime    → minimal resolver & types only
  react      → hooks only
  server     → server utilities (no watchers)
  dev        → generators & watchers
  cli        → commands

next-intlayer/
  plugin     → thin Next.js config wrapper
  server     → runtime helpers
  dev        → build/watch integration
```

Additionally:

**Lazy-load dev tools**

```ts
if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production") {
  await import("@ intlayer/chokidar");
}
```

---

### Expected Result

| Area | Current | After separation |
|----|----|----|
Runtime imports | tens of KB | single-digit KB |
Next plugin graph | ~1.6MB gz | small (<50KB expected) |
Tree-shaking | unreliable | reliable |
Edge compatibility | risky | safe |

---

### Why This Matters

i18n libraries are imported everywhere in an app.  
Any overhead multiplies across the entire project.

Separating runtime from tooling would:

- reduce bundle size significantly
- improve install/build performance
- simplify dependency graphs
- improve edge/serverless compatibility

---

If useful, I can help test a runtime-only build and provide bundle analysis feedback.

records.title: @wordpress/scripts 33.0.0 still publishes vulnerable build-tool dependencies
records.body:
## Description

A clean install of the latest `@wordpress/scripts@33.0.0` (Node 25.7.0, npm 11.10.1, no lockfile) reports 29 npm audit findings: 22 moderate and 7 high. All paths originate under `@wordpress/scripts`.

The published package metadata also appears inconsistent with the 33.0.0 changelog: the changelog says `webpack-dev-server` was updated to `^5.2.1`, but `npm view @wordpress/scripts@33.0.0 dependencies.webpack-dev-server` returns `^4.15.1`, and a clean install resolves 4.15.2.

## Reproduction

`npm init -y`
`npm install --save-dev @wordpress/scripts@33.0.0`
`npm audit --json`

Representative vulnerable paths from the clean tree:

- `@wordpress/scripts@33.0.0 > adm-zip@0.5.18` (GHSA-xcpc-8h2w-3j85; patched 0.6.0 exists)
- `@wordpress/scripts@33.0.0 > copy-webpack-plugin@10.2.4 > serialize-javascript@6.0.2` (GHSA-5c6j-r48x-rmvq and GHSA-qj8w-gfj5-8c6v)
- `@wordpress/scripts@33.0.0 > markdownlint-cli@0.31.1 > markdownlint@0.25.1 > markdown-it@12.3.2 > linkify-it@3.0.3` (multiple quadratic-complexity advisories)
- `@wordpress/scripts@33.0.0 > markdownlint-cli@0.31.1 > minimatch@3.0.8` (multiple ReDoS advisories)
- `@wordpress/scripts@33.0.0 > webpack-dev-server@4.15.2 > sockjs@0.3.24 > uuid@8.3.2` (webpack dev-server exposure/DoS advisories and GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq)
- `@wordpress/scripts@33.0.0 > @wordpress/e2e-test-utils-playwright@1.51.0 > lighthouse@12.8.2 > @sentry/node@9.47.1 > @opentelemetry/core@1.30.1` (GHSA-8988-4f7v-96qf and propagated moderate findings)

## Expected

The published latest package should carry the dependency upgrades described in its changelog and resolve patched transitive versions where compatible, without consumers needing broad `overrides` that can violate parent package constraints.

## Additional context

This was found while upgrading a WordPress plugin from scripts 31.8.0 to 33.0.0. The upgrade removes the critical finding and reduces high findings, but the latest upstream package remains the blocker for removing the residual dev-only advisories safely.

records.title: [Placement深度探索] Nested Resource Providers
records.body:
## 1. 背景概述
顾名思义，Nested Resource Providers，即嵌套的资源提供者。在Ocata版本，这个[bp/nested-resource-providers](https://specs.openstack.org/openstack/nova-specs/specs/ocata/approved/nested-resource-providers.html)就被提出，主要是为了使用户可以定义不同的Resource Provider之间的层级关系（hierarchical relationship）。

我们知道，目前Placement的功能已初具雏形，我们可以记录系统中可数的资源的总数。一个Resource Provider有一系列不同资源种类的存量信息（Inventory），也通过已分配量（Allocation）信息来记录已使用量。通过Resource Provider/Inventory/Allocation这三个关键模型，我们就可以解决以下几个需求：

1.  **每个Resource Provider有多少某种类型的资源**？通过Invetory记录，例如某个主机VCPU的总量；
2.  **系统已经消耗了多少某种类型的资源**？通过Allocation记录，例如某个虚拟机消耗了1GB的内存；
3.  **每个Resource Provider为某种类型的资源提供多少超分配的能力**？通过Inventory的allocation_ratio字段来记录。

如下图所示，一个计算节点包含8个CPU，500GB硬盘，16GB内存，已使用3个CPU，3GB硬盘，2GB内存，这个计算节点所属高IO组，具备SSD的能力，抽象为Placement模型后，若下图所示：

![placement](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1736354/35139070-699e3be0-fd2c-11e7-8172-20f2cdb6671f.jpg)

计算节点对应Resource Provider（蓝色），其包含的某种类型资源的总量对应Inventory（紫色），资源的类型对应Resource Class（灰色），已使用量对应Allocation（绿色），所属的组对应Placement组（黄色），计算节点的特质对应Trait（橙色）。

在之前的实现中，对于RP之间的关系，也仅仅支持aggregate功能。例如，某个RP可以把自己的资源，通过aggregate将RP的资源共享给同一aggregate的其他RP。这一功能对于共享存储、共享IP池之类的业务是满足需求的，但是，对于类似父子的这种关系，是无法支持的。

例如，在NUMA场景下，我们不但需要将主机的内存和VCPU资源记录，同时也需要记录每个主机上的某个NUMA的资源总量及消耗情况，这个就属于父子关系。

## 2. 存在的问题
在[nested-resource-providers][1]中提到一场景：

[1]: https://etherpad.openstack.org/p/nested-resource-providers  "nested-resource-providers的etherpad"

> there are resource classes that represent a consumable entity that is within another consumable entity. An example of such a resource class is the amount of memory "local" to a particular NUMA cell.

就是说一些类型代表一种资源消费的实体，同时，包含了另外一种资源消费的实体。举个例子就是memory这种resource class，这个memory是属于某个NUMA的。让我们通过一个例子来看下这个问题。

在一些对性能或时延有苛刻要求的场景，我们通常希望一个虚拟机能够部署到某个NUMA上（一个主机通常含有多个NUMA CELL，注意这个CELL和我们在Nova中说的Cell V2不是一个含义，而是NUMA独有的名词）。假设我们已经创建了一个叫做“NUMA_MEMORY_MB”的资源类型，资源的总量是192GB。当我们希望将它创建到一个磁盘大小充足并且NUMA内存充足的主机上时，如果仅考虑这个主机上的总内存，可能会找到一个并不是我们期望的主机。我们必须考虑每个NUMA CELL中的内存是否充足。

![numa](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1736354/35147337-321bf046-fd49-11e7-8814-3f256b4d02ad.jpg)

如上图所示，假设一个主机总共有192GB内存。其中128GB分配给了NUMA CELL0，另外64GB分配给了NUMA CELL1。

* 虚拟机A消耗了112GB内存，落在了NUMA CELL0上，NUMA CELL0还剩16GB内存
* 虚拟机B消耗了48GB内存，落在了NUMA CELL1上，NUMA CELL1还剩16GB内存
* 虚拟机C来的时候说：我需要32GB内存。我们应该如何调度主机呢？

这时，现有的Placement机制，会汇总一个Resource Provider下面所有的某种资源的总和，即会查到的是主机上总内存，发现还有32GB，调度时，就认为这个主机可以作为备选主机。然而，实际我们从上图已经可以看出，实际每个NUMA CELL可供调度的内存均只有16GB，其实是不满足要求的。



## 3. 基础的数据模型
在现有Resource Provider的基础上，实现这种嵌套关系，基础的数据模型非常重要。在关系数据库中，对分层数据进行管理，主要有2个模型：

![datamodel](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1736354/35257252-264f5338-0033-11e8-9fb3-bc25d5d7c353.jpg)

1. 邻接表（Adjacency list）。记录parent，即父节点。
2. 嵌套集合（Nested sets）。记录left和right，注意这里不是指兄弟节点，而是类似一个编号，right=left+2n+1，根节点比较特殊，left为1，right为2n，其中，n为节点的总数。

有关邻接表和嵌套模型的内容可以参考[Managing Hierarchical Data in MySQL][2]和[Join-fu: The Art of SQL][3]。

[2]: http://mikehillyer.com/articles/managing-hierarchical-data-in-mysql/ "Managing Hierarchical Data in MySQL"
[3]: http://joinfu.com/presentations/joinfu/joinfu_part_two.pdf "Join-fu: The Art of SQL"

Reousce Provider最终选择了邻接表作为基础数据结构，在[etherpad][2]中，轻描淡写的描述了下选择的原因：

> **A simple way of modeling this kind of nesting in a relational data store is to use something called an adjacency list model.** We add a NULLABLE parent_resource_provider_id column to the resource_providers table to indicate that the resource provider is either a "top-level" provider (such as a compute host) or a "nested" provider (such as a NUMA cell on the compute host).

个人认为，选择这个模型的原因除了实现比较简单外，还有就是Resource Provider嵌套层级的不是非常深，即使进行一些查询时需要left join几次，也不会有非常大的性能损耗。当然，正如Jaypipes的PPT所述那样，比起Nest Sets来说，Adjacency list是**very common but doesn't scale**。 

另外，[Managing Hierarchical Data in MySQL][2]的“LIMITATIONS OF THE ADJACENCY LIST MODEL”一节中，提到了2个这个数据结构的限制，回头看来，在Placement进行设计时，都有应对的措施：
> Working with the adjacency list model in pure SQL can be difficult at best. Before being able to see the full path of a category we have to know the level at which it resides. In addition, special care must be taken when deleting nodes because of the potential for orphaning an entire sub-tree in the process (delete the portable electronics category and all of its children are orphaned). 

其一，是Full-path的遍历（例如，获取一个父树），我们必须要多次join，并且需要知道自己在第几层，从而决定join的次数。这个在Placement，加了一个root_id进行解决。
其二，是删除父类节点时，有可能造成底下的树被孤立了，这个Placement则是通过限制用户行为来解决的，即不允许删除有子节点的父节点。

因此，最终在Resource Provider的模型中，我们新增了2个field：
1. **parent_provider_uuid**：表示Resource Provider的直接父亲节点。对于非嵌套的节点，这个field为NULL，对于嵌套的节点来说，这个字段在大多数情况可能是计算节点的UUID，表示这个资源是host下的资源；
> Indicates the UUID of the immediate parent provider. This will be None for the vast majority of providers, and for nested resource providers, this will most likely be the compute host’s UUID.
2. **root_provider_uuid**：表示这个Resource Provider是一个树形providers的根节点。这个节点可以允许我们实现一个高效的树形访问，从而避免递归地查询父子关系。
> Indicates the UUID of the resource provider that is at the “root” of the tree of providers. This field allows us to implement efficient tree-access queries and avoid use of recursive queries to follow child->parent relations.

数据模型的Patch在这: [patch/377138](https://review.openstack.org/#/c/377138)。

## 4. 核心流程解析
### 4.1 创建/删除 Nest Resource Provider
最简单的流程就是对Nest Resource Provider进行操作了，对于创建的流程来说，需要用户传递父亲节点，请求的格式类似：
```json
 {
     "name": "Shared storage",
     "parent_provider_uuid": "542df8ed-9be2-49b9-b4db-6d3183ff8ec8"
 }
```
在创建的过程中，如果包含了父亲节点，那么，我们可以很方便的找到其对应的root节点，然后填到自己的root中（子节点和父节点有相同的root）；如果没有父节点的话，那么这个子节点的根节点就是自己了（参考代码：[nova/objects/resource_provider.py#L812-L819](https://github.com/openstack/nova/blob/85a957dcd9c2e3dc8ed03f7e1f88a535bcced7f7/nova/objects/resource_provider.py#L812-L819)）。

同样的，在删除节点的时候，也需要考虑下嵌套的关系，在Resource Provider删除时，加了一个简单的限制：如果一个Resource Provider有子节点(参考代码：[nova/objects/resource_provider.py#L824-L830](https://github.com/openstack/nova/blob/85a957dcd9c2e3dc8ed03f7e1f88a535bcced7f7/nova/objects/resource_provider.py#L824-L830))，

records.title: [PCG-2.3] DAG, Pin Type, Cycle, Limit and Diagnostic Validation
records.body:
## Goal

Validate graph topology, types, capabilities and budgets before compilation.

## Scope

- Detect cycles, dangling edges, duplicate IDs, incompatible pins, unavailable nodes and declared-limit violations.
- Return stable cause chains tied to graph and node provenance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All invalid graphs reject before evaluator work begins.
- [ ] Diagnostics are deterministic, bounded and independent of unordered container traversal.
- [ ] Targeted automated coverage protects normal, boundary, failure, replacement and lifecycle behavior.
